title: Real time: WebSockets, Server-Sent Events and long polling

videos.script: A customer waits for their order to leave the warehouse. The page should change the moment it does, without the customer pressing anything. {{wait}} HTTP was not built for that. The browser asks and the server answers; the server cannot speak first. {{http}} There are four ways around it, and you will build all four on your machine: asking again and again, asking and waiting, a response that never ends, and a connection that both sides can talk on. {{four}} Polling, long polling, Server-Sent Events and WebSockets. Each one is the right answer somewhere, and the lesson shows where. {{right}} Then the problem that appears with the second server. A customer connected to one instance does not hear about an event that arrived at the other. {{second}} You will fix that with a backplane, a small piece of publish and subscribe that every instance listens to. {{backplane}} Long-held connections change what a server is. It no longer answers and forgets; it holds thousands of open conversations, and every deploy has to end them politely.
